Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
//https://www.lintcode.com/problem/binary-tree-paths/description?_from=ladder&&fromId=1
/*
Divide && Conquer 
*/


/**
 * Definition of TreeNode:
 * class TreeNode {
 * public:
 *     int val;
 *     TreeNode *left, *right;
 *     TreeNode(int val) {
 *         this->val = val;
 *         this->left = this->right = NULL;
 *     }
 * }
 */

class Solution
{
public:
    /**
     * @param root: the root of the binary tree
     * @return: all root-to-leaf paths
     */
    vector<string> binaryTreePaths(TreeNode *root)
    {
        vector<string> res;
        if (NULL == root)
        {
            return res;
        }

        if (NULL == root->left && NULL == root->right)
        {
            res.push_back(to_string(root->val));
            return res;
        }

        vector<string> left = binaryTreePaths(root->left);
        vector<string> right = binaryTreePaths(root->right);

        for (auto &e : left)
        {
            res.push_back(to_string(root->val) + "->" + e);
        }

        for (auto &e : right)
        {
            res.push_back(to_string(root->val) + "->" + e);
        }
        return res;
    }
};
